newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - US debt vols supported as big week looms.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - US debt vols supported as big week looms.

text.p: U.S. interest rate options volatilities were a touch lower Friday but remained underpinned by anticipation of next week's heavy report lineup, analysts said.
They noted implied volatilities for options on Treasury bond futures this week climbed out of a trough and back toward the middle of historical norms.

On the day, June rose to 9.3 percent when the underlying futures moved to the session lows, but ended around 9.2 percent, steady with Thursday, as the market factored in weekend time decay, said a broker for a U.S. trading firm.

Implied volatilities in the short end of the yield curve pulled back after posting steady gains earlier in the week, Eurodollar floor brokers said. Late in the session, September Eurodollar volatility was steady at 11.2 percent and December was down 0.4 point at 12.6 percent.
Short-dated June midcurve volatility fell 1.2 point to 16.0 percent while September was steady at 16.6 percent.
Open interest in Eurodollar options is on the rise, especially in the midcurves, where interest in puts is outpacing that of calls, said Howard Gussis, floor analyst with ABN Amro.

Midcurve options expire in 1997 but are priced from 1998 futures. Gussis said bigger price swings in the deferred futures makes the short-dated options particularly attractive. "All the action is in the midcurves," he said. "Everybody likes these cheap speculative plays."
In Treasury bond options, it was the calm before the storm as traders braced for the week ahead. "It has been one of our quieter weeks in a while," said one bond floor broker.
June bond futures ended at 107-04, down 6/32.

That should change next week, traders said, when a concentration of economic data, spanning Tuesday's first-quarter employment cost index to Friday's April employment data, has the potential to roil prices and stir up volatility.

Among the larger trades going through the bond options pit today, a U.S. commission house bought 2,000 June 104-00 puts, a second brokerage bought 2,000 December 116-00 calls, and a European banking firm bought 1,000 June 109-00 calls.
